rationale:
Today's slate has 5 pieces: 1 long-form, 3 Shorts and 1 carousel. Every piece is about GLP-1 and covers 5 different pillars (research, get-the-most, how-it-works, myths, life-on-glp1). The body systems are muscle, brain reward, eye and digestion, and only L1 and S1 share one (muscle).

**Trend mix**
- Emerging or rising (be early): L1, S1, S2, S3.
- Evergreen with a timely hook: C1, Halloween eating habits.
- Calm myth correction: S3 on vision loss, a caution topic handled evidence-first.

**How the analytics shaped it**
- L1 and S1 use the headline-decoder format with a named next-gen drug plus the verified number and its comparator. It's 2 for 2 so far (long-form 112, Short 53).
- S2 copies our best Short (113 views): a search-style question about a named drug that answers honestly, "mostly in animals".
- S3 is a safety question with a named drug, a regulator's own number and the exact population.
- Every title leads with a named drug. None uses "GLP-1" alone as the subject.

**Spin-off and length test**
- S1 is the spin-off of L1.
- S2 is our cleanest candidate for the overdue 35–50s length test.

**Skipped**
- Repeats within 30 days: hair loss and the NYU genetics study (long-form 09-28), nails (09-28 and 10-01), the kidney REMODEL study (carousel 10-05), survodutide (10-05), ACHIEVE-4 (Short 10-01), retatrutide approval (Short 09-30), stopping a GLP-1 (long-form 09-29).
- Psoriasis, women's nutrients, pregnancy and postpartum stay in the queue for later days.
- Nothing the radar marked reject was available, so nothing needed excluding on that basis.

pieces.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide: Regeneron's Phase 2 COURAGE final results. Lean-mass loss was 4.2% vs 7.3% on semaglutide + placebo at 52 weeks (75 mg arm). Investigational, company-reported conference data, not yet peer-reviewed.
pieces.angle: Title: 'Trevogrumab + Semaglutide: 4.2% vs 7.3% Lean-Mass Loss at 52 Weeks, Obesity (Phase 2)' (under 100 characters). First 15s: '42% less' means 4.2% vs 7.3% of lean mass lost at 52 weeks, 75 mg arm vs semaglutide + placebo, adults with BMI 30+. Company-reported at EASD 2026, in press at The Lancet, investigational. Lean mass is not pure muscle. No strength or function data yet. Pivot to protein (with the kidney caveat) and strength training. Mention GI side effects. Exact prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: Can Trevogrumab Stop Semaglutide Muscle Loss? 4.2% vs 7.3% Lean Mass in Phase 2
pieces.why: Fresh Regeneron data (~Oct 1) with little creator coverage. It sits on one of the most-searched GLP-1 worries and fits our best long-form formula: a named next-gen drug decoded with its number and comparator. | fact-check: Checked against Regeneron's release from 1 Oct 2026 (https://investor.regeneron.com/news-releases/news-release-details/phase-2-courage-trial-confirms-trevogrumab-prevents-lean-mass; mirror: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/REGN/phase-2-courage-trial-confirms-trevogrumab-prevents-lean-mass-and-yckn8zkxi8ay.html). Lean mass measured by DXA at 52 weeks fell 7.3% on placebo + semaglutide, 5.8% on trevogrumab 25 mg + semaglutide and 4.2% on 75 mg + semaglutide. Regeneron calls that 20.5% and 42.5% 'relative preservation'. The population is adults with obesity (BMI 30 or higher). Results were presented at EASD 2026. Fixes: (1) The release says the paper is 'in press with The Lancet', so 'not yet peer-reviewed' is out of date. Say 'accepted by The Lancet, not yet published; figures from Regeneron's release'. (2) The release doesn't say the 25 mg arm 'was not significant'. Only say that if the release or paper states it; otherwise say 'smaller effect (5.8% vs 7.3%)'. (3) The release extract has no arm sizes, no total weight or fat loss per arm and no discontinuation rates. Use them only if a primary source reports them. Otherwise say 'not reported yet' and never estimate. (4) Adverse events: at least one in 77% on trevogrumab vs 82% on placebo + semaglutide. Most common: nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting. (5) The thigh MRI figure (about 69-72% preservation) comes from a subset with usable scans; label it that way. (6) Don't echo Regeneron's 'prevents' wording, since lean mass still fell 4.2%. No strength or function data were reported. (7) Fix the title: 'Stop' overclaims. (8) Funder: Regeneron. The trial is investigational (trials only as of Oct 2026). Frame the STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 DXA anchors as separate trials. Keep the protein caveat for kidney disease.

pieces.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide COURAGE result in one idea: what the '42% less muscle loss' headline means in absolute numbers
pieces.angle: Title: 'Trevogrumab + Semaglutide: 4.2% vs 7.3% Lean-Mass Loss? #shorts'. On-screen qualifier: 'Phase 2 · 75 mg arm vs semaglutide + placebo · 52 wks · adults with BMI 30+ · company-reported, in press at The Lancet · investigational'. Pivot: protein (unless your clinician has told you to limit it, e.g. kidney disease) and strength training. Brief GI line. Exact prescriber line. 35-50s.
pieces.working_title: Semaglutide Muscle Loss: Did Trevogrumab Cut It to 4.2% vs 7.3%? #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1 that drives traffic to the long video. It uses the decoder formula with a named drug and a stated number, and turns a relative headline into absolute numbers. | fact-check: Same verified numbers as L1: 4.2% (75 mg) vs 5.8% (25 mg) vs 7.3% (placebo + semaglutide) lean-mass loss at 52 weeks, adults with BMI 30+. Fixes: (1) Change 'not peer-reviewed' to 'in press at The Lancet, not yet published'. (2) Drop 'lower dose didn't reach significance' unless the primary source states it. (3) The current title can read as if trevogrumab caused the 4.2% on its own; the safer title names the comparator. (4) Keep 'lean mass (not pure muscle)' on screen. Common AEs: nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting. Never suggest any source of the drug.

pieces.topic: Why semaglutide may quiet 'food noise': GLP-1 lowers 'wanting' (dopamine-driven drive) more than 'liking' (pleasure). Wake Forest reward-system research, mostly in animals.
pieces.angle: Title: 'Does Semaglutide (Ozempic) Make Food Less Enjoyable? Wanting vs Liking #shorts'. Answer within 10s: in mice, GLP-1 drugs mainly turn down the urge to seek food ('wanting'). The pleasure of eating ('liking') seems less affected. This isn't proven in people yet. Label every finding 'in mice' or 'in people', with a primary source on each. 'Food noise' only as the term people use. Close: eat slowly and stop at comfortably full. Nausea line. Exact prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: Does Ozempic Make Food Less Enjoyable? Wanting vs Liking #shorts
pieces.why: Wake Forest piece from Oct 5. It copies our #1 GLP-1 Short format (a named-drug mechanism question answered honestly, 'only in animals so far'), and it's a good candidate for the length test. | fact-check: I couldn't verify the 'Wake Forest' attribution. The reward-circuit research I found is mostly in mice: 2026 work showing GLP-1 drugs reduce hedonic feeding via the central amygdala and lower dopamine release (https://www.news-medical.net/news/20260506/GLP-1-weight-loss-drugs-modulate-brain-reward-circuits-to-suppress-eating-for-pleasure.aspx), and animal work where semaglutide reduced cue-driven food seeking while dopamine responses during eating were preserved (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2772408523029071). 'Wanting vs liking' is a reasonable reading of that evidence, but it's a hypothesis, not proven in humans. Fixes: (1) Remove 'Wake Forest' unless the scriptwriter cites a specific primary paper from there. (2) Give each finding a source tag plus 'in mice' or 'in people'. (3) The honest answer is 'not proven in humans', not a 'yes'. (4) Mention nausea briefly. The 35-50s length test with a named-drug title is fine.

pieces.topic: Semaglutide and sudden vision loss (NAION): the Austin father's Wegovy story vs what regulators say (EMA 2025: very rare side effect, up to 1 in 10,000 users)
pieces.angle: Title: 'Can Semaglutide (Wegovy, Ozempic) Affect Eyesight? What EMA Says About NAION #shorts'. Within 10s: Europe's regulator lists NAION as a very rare possible side effect, affecting up to 1 in 10,000 people on semaglutide. As of Oct 2026, US labels don't list it and FDA says it is evaluating. Studies disagree on cause. Shared risk factors: diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea. Sudden vision change: same-day urgent care, tell your prescriber, don't stop on your own. Exact prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: Can Semaglutide (Wegovy) Cause Vision Loss? What Regulators Say #shorts
pieces.why: Rising fear-driven searches (KXAN/Yahoo, Oct 5) where law-firm pages dominate the results. It's a safety question with a named drug and a regulator's number. This is a caution topic, so the angle is evidence-first; it's today's myth-busting slot. | fact-check: Verified: EMA's PRAC concluded in June 2025 that NAION is a 'very rare' side effect of semaglutide (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy), affecting up to 1 in 10,000 people (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/prac-concludes-eye-condition-naion-very-rare-side-effect-semaglutide-medicines-ozempic-rybelsus-wegovy). The EMA says observational studies in adults with type 2 diabetes suggest about a 2-fold relative risk, roughly 1 extra case per 10,000 person-years. FDA status: a 29 Sep 2026 report says US labels for Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus and Mounjaro still don't list NAION, and FDA lists it as a potential signal it is 'evaluating' (https://www.medicaldaily.com/fda-glp1-naion-signal-us-label-warning-review-479225). That is a secondary source, so hedge it. Fixes: (1) Never say 'FDA warning'. Say 'as of Oct 2026, US labels don't list NAION; FDA says it is evaluating'. (2) I couldn't verify the Austin father's story. Drop it or mention it generically ('recent news reports'), with no names and no dramatised imagery. (3) Keep the claim to semaglutide only; the EMA ruling doesn't cover tirzepatide. (4) Say 'linked to' or 'listed as a possible very rare side effect', not 'causes'. (5) Don't paraphrase the EMA's 'stop if confirmed' line as viewer advice; that's the doctor's decision. Red flag: sudden vision loss means same-day urgent care (911/999 if sudden and severe). Don't stop the medicine on your own.

pieces.topic: Halloween treats on semaglutide or tirzepatide: why very sweet or greasy treats may sit differently (slower stomach emptying, nausea triggers) and portion-friendly habits
pieces.angle: Title: 'Halloween on Semaglutide or Tirzepatide: 4 Tips for an Easier Stomach'. Same 9-slide structure. Each habit carries a verified guidance source tag. Use 'can slow stomach emptying' and 'some people find'.
pieces.working_title: Halloween Treats on Semaglutide or Tirzepatide: 7 Tips for an Easier Stomach
pieces.why: The seasonal cycle started Oct 5 (People.com). Publishing now lets it rank before the Oct 31 peak. It's an evergreen side-effect topic with a timely hook and a list people will save. | fact-check: Safe, useful topic. The title promises '7 Tips' but the slides deliver 4 habits plus a red-flag slide and a prescriber slide. Fix the title count or add tips. Slide 2: the gastric-emptying effect is strongest early and can lessen over time, so say 'can slow'. Slide 3: tag to the prescribing information or NHS/manufacturer patient advice (smaller meals, avoid greasy foods if nauseous) and keep 'some people'. Slide 7: keep 'unless you've been told to limit fluids'. Slide 8: give the pancreatitis red flag in full, with 911/999 and ER/A&E. No weight, guilt or restriction language, and no candy-as-'cheat' framing. Caption opens with digestion framing, no brand hashtags, exact prescriber line.
